mainTopic: Who may eat קדשים and the קרבן פסח on the night of עֶרֶב פסח: the end of the משנה about an אונן and one who gathers bones, the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל about a גר who converted on עֶרֶב פסח, and the גמרא's first explanations.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה from the previous daf. A bone-gatherer may immerse and eat קדשים at night, and בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a גר who converted on ערב פסח. The גמרא explains why an אונן may eat the פסח but not other קדשים at night. Mourning at night is only rabbinic, and the רבנן did not uphold their rule where the כרת of the פסח is at stake. It then rereads the bone-gatherer case: other people gathered the bones for him, so he is not טמא מת. Next, רבי יוחנן limits the convert dispute to a ערל גוי. He explains that בית הלל made a גזירה so the convert will not wrongly immerse and eat the same day after real טומאת מת next year, and a ברייתא confirms this. רבא then lists three rabbinic rules that stand even though a person will miss the פסח: the convert, sprinkling, and the מילה knife. He also lists three rules that give way: the אונן, the מצורע, and the בית הפרס. The גמרא gives a source for each case, including רבי יוחנן's teaching that the ban on a טבול יום entering מחנה לויה is only rabbinic. The source for בית הפרס continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The bone-gatherer may eat sacrificial food at night
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its list: one whose relatives' bones are being gathered may immerse and eat קדשים in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who gathers bones for himself immerses and eats sacrificial food.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a משנה that began on the previous daf. It says that the person involved in gathering his parents' bones may immerse and eat קדשים that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה said an אונן may eat only the פסח at night, not other קדשים. Here it adds that a person whose mourning is lighter, because it is only rabbinic even during the day, may eat all קדשים at night. The גמרא will soon question whether a person who actually gathered bones can really be pure enough to do this.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gathers the bones of a dead relative to move them to a permanent grave
Immerses in a מקוה
Sacrificial food (other than the קרבן פסח)
A mourner on the day a close relative died

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the end of a list that started on the previous daf with the אונן and השומע על מתו.

phrases.english: And one who gathers bones for himself —
phrases.notes: Gathering the bones of parents for reburial; this creates a rabbinic day of mourning.

phrases.english: immerses and eats sacrificial food.
phrases.notes: Even regular קדשים, not only the פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמְלַקֵּט לוֹ עֲצָמוֹת טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל בַּקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the משנה from the previous daf (list of mourners).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bone-gatherer may immerse and eat קדשים at night.

steps.title: A convert on Passover eve: dispute of the two schools
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say a גר who converted on עֶרֶב פסח may immerse and eat the פסח that night. בית הלל say he is like someone leaving a grave and must go through seven-day purification.
steps.simpleTranslation: A convert who converted on ערב פסח: בית שמאי say he immerses and eats his קרבן פסח in the evening. בית הלל say one who separates from the foreskin is like one who separates from the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new case, a non-Jew who converts on the day before Pesach. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about whether he can eat the קרבן פסח that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, the convert only needs to immerse and can eat that same evening. According to בית הלל, the רבנן treated him like someone who touched a dead body, so he needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days and cannot eat this year's פסח. The גמרא explains below, in step 8, that this is a rabbinic decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who converted
The day before פסח (the 14th of ניסן)
The school of שמאי
The school of הלל
One who separates from the foreskin, meaning one who was just circumcised as part of conversion
Like one who separates from a grave, meaning he is treated as טמא מת

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the classic מחלוקות of בית שמאי and בית הלל, and it shows that the רבנן could impose a status of טומאה even on a brand-new convert.

phrases.english: A convert who converted on Passover eve,
Beit Shammai say:
he immerses and eats his Paschal lamb in the evening,
and Beit Hillel say:
one who separates from the foreskin
phrases.notes: Becomes circumcised as part of conversion.

phrases.english: is like one who separates from the grave.
phrases.notes: He needs the seven-day purification for טומאת מת.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר בְּעֶרֶב פֶּסַח בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the same משנה, about who may eat the פסח at night.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the convert immerses and eats the פסח. בית הלל: he is treated like one leaving a grave and needs seven-day purification.

steps.title: Why may a mourner eat the פסח but not other offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's rule that an אונן eats the פסח at night but not other קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the משנה made this rule. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question goes back to the first ruling of the משנה, from the previous daf. An אונן may eat the פסח at night but not other קדשים, so the גמרא wants to know why these two are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
What is the reason?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the convert, which was just mentioned. It is about the אונן from the start of the משנה.

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The reason an אונן may eat the פסח at night but not other קדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening ruling of the משנה about the אונן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the אונן is allowed to eat the פסח at night but forbidden to eat other קדשים.

steps.title: Night mourning is rabbinic and gives way before כרת
steps.stepSummary: Mourning on the night after the death is only rabbinic. The רבנן did not enforce it against the פסח, which carries כרת, but did enforce it against other קדשים, which are only a positive מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that mourning at night is rabbinic. Regarding the פסח, they did not uphold their words where there is כרת. Regarding other offerings, they upheld their words where there is only a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. Night-time אנינות is only rabbinic, and the רבנן relaxed it for the פסח but not for other קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, אנינות lasts only for the day of death, so the night after is only rabbinic. Not bringing the פסח is punished with כרת, so the רבנן did not let their decree block it. Not eating other קדשים only misses a מצות עשה, so their decree stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: The mourner's status during the night after the day of death
Of rabbinic origin (not Torah law)
They did not uphold their decree
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for not bringing the פסח
A positive commandment (here, eating קדשים)

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic decree may give way where keeping it would cause a loss involving כרת. It stays in force where only a מצות עשה is lost.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general principle used across ש״ס: how strong a rabbinic decree is depends on how severe the Torah obligation it would block.

phrases.english: He holds that acute mourning at night is rabbinic,
and with regard to the Pesach, they did not uphold their words
in a place of karet,
with regard to sacrificial food, they upheld their words
in a place of a positive commandment.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Night אנינות is rabbinic. The רבנן waived it where כרת is at stake (פסח) but kept it where only a מצות עשה is at stake (other קדשים).

steps.title: How can a bone-gatherer be pure the same night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: someone who gathers bones touched a dead body and needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days, so how can he eat קדשים that night?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who hears about his dead,' etc. One who gathers bones? But he needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the late-news mourner and the bone-gatherer. It then attacks the bone-gatherer case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who handles human bones becomes טמא מת. טומאת מת cannot be removed by a single immersion; it needs the ashes of the פרה אדומה sprinkled on the third and seventh days. So he could not eat קדשים that same night, as the משנה seems to say.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hears about his relative's death (late news, after thirty days)
Sprinkling (of the פרה אדומה ashes) on the third and seventh days
Impurity from contact with a corpse

phrases.english: 'One who hears about his dead,' etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: One who gathers bones?
phrases.notes: Said in surprise.

phrases.english: But he needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the bone-gatherer may immerse and eat קדשים at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Touching bones causes טומאת מת, which requires a seven-day purification with sprinkling, so a same-day immersion cannot be enough.

steps.title: Read it as: others gathered the bones for him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by rereading the משנה: it means a person whose relatives' bones were gathered by others, so he never touched them and is not טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: one for whom they gathered bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by changing how we read the משנה's words. Other people gathered the bones, not the mourner himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourner still keeps a rabbinic day of mourning because his parents' bones were moved. Since he never touched them, he has no טומאת מת. So immersion alone is enough, and he may eat קדשים that night.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)
That they (others) gathered for him

steps.whatToRemember: The bone-gatherer in the משנה is someone for whom others gathered the bones. He mourns by rabbinic law but is not טמא, so he may eat קדשים that night.

phrases.english: Say: one for whom they gathered bones.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text of the משנה (אימא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to describe a person who himself handled the bones and became טמא מת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a person for whom others gathered the bones. He has rabbinic mourning but no טומאה.

steps.title: The argument is only about a non-Jew who converts
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל is only about a ערל גוי, a non-Jew who converts on עֶרֶב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's case of 'a convert who converted': רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that the argument is about an uncircumcised non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the convert. It now defines which case the two schools are actually arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of בית הלל, that he is like someone leaving a grave, could have been read as applying to anyone who just had a מילה. רבי יוחנן narrows it. The argument is only about someone who was a גוי until today. The next steps explain why that detail matters.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert who converted (the opening words of the משנה)
A disagreement, a dispute
An uncircumcised non-Jew (here, one who converts)
Etc., meaning the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: 'A convert who converted' etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the opening words of the משנה

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is about an uncircumcised non-Jew,
phrases.notes: He was circumcised and converted on עֶרֶב פסח

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּעָרֵל גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אונן discussion (steps 3–6) and returns to the convert case in the משנה (step 2)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל applies only to a non-Jew who converts on עֶרֶב פסח.

steps.title: Why בית הלל make a rule: fear of a mistake next year
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל make a גזירה. Next year the convert might become truly טמא from a dead body. He might then think he can immerse and eat that same day, as he did this year. He would not realize that last year, as a גוי, he could not become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל hold that this is a rabbinic decree. They fear he will become טמא next year and say: 'Last year, didn't I immerse and eat? Now too I will immerse and eat.' He does not know that last year he was a non-Jew and could not become טמא. Now he is a Jew and can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind בית הלל's strict ruling. It is a protective rule made by the rabbis, not a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the new convert is not טמא at all. As a גוי he could not receive טומאת מת, so he could eat that very night. The rabbis still made him wait seven days. This way he will not wrongly 'learn' that immersing on the same day is enough after touching the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rabbinic decree
Last year
Able to become ritually impure
I immersed (in a מקוה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the convert is actually טמא by Torah law. A גוי cannot receive טומאת מת from the Torah. The seven-day wait is only a rabbinic safeguard against a future mistake.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the rule depends on him having been a גוי. That is exactly why the dispute is limited to a ערל גוי.

phrases.english: For Beit Hillel hold:
It is a decree, lest he become impure the following year,
phrases.notes: From a dead body, before פסח

phrases.english: and he will say: Last year,
did I not immerse and eat?
Now too I will immerse and eat.
But he does not know that last year —
he was a non-Jew and could not become impure,
while now he is a Jew and can become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִטָּמֵא לְשָׁנָה הַבָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יוחנן limited the dispute to a ערל גוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל's seven-day requirement is a rabbinic גזירה to stop the convert from mistakenly immersing and eating the same day after real טומאת מת in a later year.

steps.title: בית שמאי make no decree, and everyone agrees about an uncircumcised Jew
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי do not make this גזירה. Everyone agrees that a ערל ישראל who gets a מילה on עֶרֶב פסח may immerse and eat the פסח that night. The rabbis did not extend the rule to him because of the convert case.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that we do not make the decree. But an uncircumcised Jew, all agree, immerses and eats his פסח in the evening. We do not decree on an uncircumcised Jew because of an uncircumcised non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's view and then states the case where there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An uncircumcised Jew was always able to become טמא. So there is no false lesson about last year that he could learn. The rabbis also chose not to add a second decree on him just because his case looks like the convert's.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not make a decree
An uncircumcised Jew (for example, one whose מילה was delayed for health reasons)
Everyone agrees
His קרבן פסח

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai hold: we do not make a decree.
But an uncircumcised Jew —
all agree that he immerses and eats
his Paschal offering in the evening,
and we do not decree on an uncircumcised Jew
because of an uncircumcised non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation by giving בית שמאי's view and the case both sides agree on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערל ישראל circumcised on עֶרֶב פסח may immerse and eat the פסח that night according to everyone, and he is not included in the convert's גזירה.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the argument is only about a convert
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the same thing. The schools agree about a ערל ישראל and argue only about a ערל גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about an uncircumcised Jew, who immerses and eats his פסח in the evening. What did they argue about? About an uncircumcised non-Jew. בית שמאי say he immerses and eats his פסח in the evening. בית הלל say one who separates from the foreskin is like one who separates from the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright what רבי יוחנן said. There is no argument about a ערל ישראל, and the argument is only about a ערל גוי. It also repeats בית הלל's comparison of the convert to someone leaving a grave.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
They did not disagree
One who separates from the foreskin (a convert just circumcised)
Like one who separates from a grave, so he needs seven-day purification

steps.whatToRemember: The argument in the משנה is only about a non-Jew who converts on עֶרֶב פסח. בית הלל require seven days of purification as a rabbinic safeguard, so he will not get confused next year. A Jew circumcised late may immerse and eat that night according to everyone.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about an uncircumcised Jew
that he immerses and eats his Paschal offering in the evening.
About what did they disagree?
About an uncircumcised non-Jew.
For Beit Shammai say:
he immerses and eats his Paschal offering in the evening,
and Beit Hillel say:
one who separates from the foreskin
is like one who separates from the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up the scope given in steps 7–9
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the dispute is only about a ערל גוי and that all agree about a ערל ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that says this outright

steps.title: רבא lists when rabbinic rules stand against כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists three cases where the rabbis kept their rule even though it caused someone to miss the פסח, which carries כרת. He then lists three cases where they did not keep their rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: For a convert who was a ערל, for sprinkling, and for the מילה knife, the rabbis kept their rule even in a situation of כרת. For an אונן, a מצורע, and a בית הפרס, they did not keep their rule in a situation of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new general list. It sorts rabbinic rules into two groups: rules that stay in force even if a person will miss the פסח, and rules that are set aside so he can bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Missing the קרבן פסח carries the punishment of כרת. Normally we might think a rabbinic rule should give way so a person can avoid that. רבא teaches that in three cases the rabbis still held firm, but in three other cases they relaxed their rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They upheld their words, meaning the rabbis kept their decree in force
In a situation of כרת, here meaning a case where the person would miss the קרבן פסח
A mourner on the day a close relative died
A person with צרעת, a spiritual skin affliction
A field where a grave was plowed over, so bone pieces may be scattered in it

steps.confusionAlert: "They upheld their words in a situation of כרת" does NOT mean the rabbis allowed someone to commit a sin that carries כרת. It means they kept their rule even though it would stop him from bringing the פסח, which is a מצוה whose neglect carries כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets up the next several lines. The גמרא will now explain each case one by one.

phrases.english: Rava said:
An uncircumcised convert, sprinkling, and the circumcision scalpel:
phrases.notes: Three cases where the rabbis held firm.

phrases.english: They upheld their words even in a place of karet.
An acute mourner, a leper, and a beit haperas:
phrases.notes: Three cases where the rabbis gave way.

phrases.english: They did not uphold their words in a place of karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It generalizes the principle from step 4 (a rabbinic rule versus כרת) and the בית הלל decree from steps 8–9 into a list of cases where the rabbis did or did not hold firm against the כרת of the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbinic rules about the convert, sprinkling, and the מילה knife stand even if the person misses the פסח. The rules about an אונן, a מצורע, and a בית הפרס give way so he can bring it.

steps.title: The convert case is the one already discussed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ערל case is the convert case we just learned about from בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a ערל is what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining רבא's list. It points back to the convert case discussed a moment ago.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל ruled that a convert on ערב פסח may not immerse and eat the פסח that night, as a גזירה. This stops him from bringing the פסח even though missing it carries כרת. So this is a clear case where the rabbis held firm.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we said, pointing back to an earlier discussion
Uncircumcised; here, a non-Jew who converts on ערב פסח

phrases.english: Uncircumcised: as we have said.
phrases.notes: Refers to the בית הלל decree in steps 7–9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the first item in רבא's list.
steps.raayaObject: The first case in רבא's list, the convert
steps.raayaSupportSource: The בית הלל decree quoted by רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Sprinkling does not override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The source for the sprinkling case is a teaching that הזאה is forbidden as a rabbinic rule and does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sprinkling: as the Master said, sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition, and it does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second item, sprinkling. It quotes a teaching that sprinkling the purifying water is forbidden on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is טמא מת needs sprinkling on his seventh day. If that day is ערב פסח and it falls on שבת, he cannot be sprinkled, so he cannot eat the פסח. The ban on sprinkling is only rabbinic, yet the rabbis still kept it even though he will miss the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the ashes of the red cow mixed with water, to purify someone טמא מת
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת
Overrides or pushes aside
As the Master said, introducing a known teaching

phrases.english: Sprinkling: as the Master said:
Sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition
phrases.notes: It is not forbidden by the Torah itself.

phrases.english: and it does not override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the second item in רבא's list.
steps.raayaObject: The second case in רבא's list, sprinkling
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching quoted as "דאמר מר": sprinkling is a שבות and does not override שבת

steps.title: The circumcision knife may not be carried
steps.stepSummary: The source for the איזמל case is a ברייתא: the מילה knife may not be carried on שבת, even through areas that are only rabbinically forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The knife: as a ברייתא teaches. Just as we may not bring it through a רשות הרבים, so too we may not bring it through roofs, courtyards, or enclosures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third item, the מילה knife. It quotes a ברייתא that forbids carrying it on שבת, even along routes where carrying is only a rabbinic ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מילה itself may be done on שבת. However, if the knife was not brought ahead of time, the rabbis still forbid carrying it through roofs and courtyards. Then the baby stays uncircumcised on ערב פסח, and his father cannot bring the פסח. The rabbis kept their rule anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The knife used for מילה
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden by the Torah
Roofs
Courtyards
Large fenced enclosures where carrying is rabbinically forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: In all three cases (the convert, sprinkling, and the knife), a rabbinic rule stays in force even though it causes a person to miss the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: The scalpel: as it was taught:
Just as we may not bring it
through a public domain,
phrases.notes: This is a Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: so too we may not bring it

phrases.aramaic: דֶּרֶךְ גַּגּוֹת וְדֶרֶךְ חֲצֵרוֹת וְדֶרֶךְ קַרְפֵּיפוֹת.
phrases.english: through roofs, through courtyards, and through enclosures.
phrases.notes: These are only rabbinic prohibitions, yet they still apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the third item in רבא's list.
steps.raayaObject: The third case in רבא's list, the מילה knife
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding carrying the איזמל even through roofs, courtyards, and enclosures

steps.title: The source for the mourner case is our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The first case in רבא's second list, the אונן, is the case already taught in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mourner case is the one we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins showing where each case in רבא's second list comes from. For the אונן, it simply points back to our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה taught that an אונן immerses and eats his פסח in the evening. By Torah law, being an אונן ends at nightfall. The rabbis normally extend it into the night, but here they let that rule go so he would not lose the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day of a close relative's death, before burial
That which we already said

phrases.english: The mourner —
phrases.notes: First item in רבא's list of cases where the rabbis did not keep their rule.

phrases.english: is that which we said.
phrases.notes: It refers back to our משנה: an אונן immerses and eats his פסח in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving sources for the first list (steps 12–14), the גמרא turns to the second list.
steps.raayaObject: The אונן case in רבא's second list

steps.title: The source for the leper case: a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The מצורע case is a ברייתא. A מצורע whose eighth day falls on ערב פסח, and who had a קרי that day, immerses and eats the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the leper case? As a ברייתא teaches: a מצורע whose eighth day falls on ערב פסח, and who had a seminal emission that same day, immerses and eats the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case רבא meant by 'מצורע,' and answers by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On his eighth day a מצורע brings קרבנות and must come to the Temple area to finish his purification. A קרי that same day makes him impure again. He can immerse, but he stays a טבול יום until nightfall. The ברייתא rules that he still immerses, finishes his purification, and eats the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת who must go through an eight-day purification process
The eighth day, when the מצורע brings his קרבנות
A seminal emission, which makes a person impure
Immerses in a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: Immersing does not make him fully pure right away. After immersion he is a טבול יום until nightfall, and that is exactly the problem the next line deals with.

phrases.english: The leper — what is it?
phrases.notes: Which case did רבא have in mind?

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
A leper whose eighth day fell
phrases.notes: The day he brings his קרבנות and finishes becoming pure.

phrases.english: on the eve of Pesach,
and he saw a seminal emission on that day —
phrases.notes: This makes him newly impure.

phrases.english: he immerses and eats.
phrases.notes: He immerses, finishes his purification, and eats the פסח at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second item in רבא's second list.
steps.raayaObject: The מצורע case in רבא's second list
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a מצורע on ערב פסח

steps.title: The Sages allow him in because the מצוה with כרת wins
steps.stepSummary: Although a טבול יום normally may not enter, this man may. A מצוה carrying כרת (the פסח) pushes aside a מצוה without כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said: even though a person who immersed today normally may not enter, this one may enter. Better that a positive מצוה with כרת come and push aside a positive מצוה without כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains why the מצורע may enter even though he is a טבול יום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a clash between two מצוות. One is the פסח, a positive מצוה whose neglect carries כרת. The other is the rule keeping impure people out of the camp, a positive מצוה without כרת. The more serious מצוה wins, so he may enter the Temple area.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who immersed today but is not fully pure until nightfall
Enters (here, the Temple area)
It is better
A positive מצוה (a 'do' command)
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for skipping the פסח

phrases.english: The Sages said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁטְּבוּל יוֹם אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס,
phrases.english: Even though one who immersed that day does not enter,
phrases.notes: The normal rule: a טבול יום stays out of the Temple area until nightfall.

phrases.english: this one enters.
phrases.notes: An exception for this מצורע on ערב פסח.

phrases.aramaic: מוּטָב יָבֹא עֲשֵׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: Better that a positive mitzvah that has כרת come,
phrases.notes: The קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: and push aside a positive mitzvah that has no כרת.
phrases.notes: The מצוה to send impure people out of the camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁטְּבוּל יוֹם אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and gives its reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טבול יום מצורע may enter on ערב פסח, because a מצוה with כרת overrides a מצוה without כרת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ban on a טבול יום is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that by Torah law there is not even a positive מצוה keeping a טבול יום out of מחנה לויה. He proves this from the 'new courtyard' in the days of יהושפט, when the rule was newly made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: by Torah law there is not even a positive מצוה involved. The verse says 'יהושפט stood in the congregation of יהודה and ירושלים, in the house of ה׳, before the new courtyard.' What is the 'new courtyard'? It means they made something new there and said: a טבול יום may not enter the camp of the Levites.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds that keeping a טבול יום out of the Temple Mount is not a Torah rule at all. It was enacted by the rabbis, as hinted in a verse about יהושפט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the מצורע fits רבא's list of rabbinic rules that were set aside. The ban on a טבול יום entering מחנה לויה is a rabbinic decree from יהושפט's time, called 'new' because it was newly enacted. So here the rabbis waived their own rule to keep a person from losing the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
The 'new courtyard'
That they made something new (enacted)
The camp of the Levites, the Temple Mount area
A king of יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: The מצורע case belongs in רבא's list because the ban on a טבול יום entering מחנה לויה is only rabbinic (from יהושפט's time). The rabbis let it go so he would not miss the פסח and its כרת.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא spoke of one עשה pushing aside another, as if the ban were Torah law. רבי יוחנן goes further: by Torah law there is not even an עשה here. That is why this case counts as a rabbinic rule being waived.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that every case on רבא's second list really involves a rabbinic rule set aside to protect the פסח.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה אֲפִילּוּ עֲשֵׂה אֵין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: By Torah law, there is not even a positive מצוה in it,
phrases.notes: Meaning there is no Torah ban at all on a טבול יום entering מחנה לויה.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"And Yehoshafat stood in the congregation of Yehudah and Yerushalayim
in the house of ה׳, before the new courtyard" (II Chronicles 20:5),
What is 'the new courtyard'?
phrases.notes: The courtyard was not physically new, so why call it that?

phrases.english: That they made something new in it, and said:

phrases.aramaic: טְבוּל יוֹם לֹא יִכָּנֵס בְּמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה.
phrases.english: One who immersed that day may not enter the camp of the Levites.
phrases.notes: A newly enacted rabbinic rule, not a Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה אֲפִילּוּ עֲשֵׂה אֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the ברייתא and shows that the rule being set aside is only rabbinic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law a טבול יום may enter מחנה לויה. The ban is a rabbinic decree from יהושפט's time.
steps.raayaObject: That the ban on a טבול יום in מחנה לויה is rabbinic

steps.title: Source for the בית הפרס case begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the next case in רבא's list, בית הפרס, and starts quoting its source: a משנה where בית שמאי and בית הלל agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of בית הפרס comes from what we learned in a משנה: 'And בית שמאי and בית הלל agree...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third case in רבא's second list, בית הפרס, and begins quoting the משנה that is its source. This line sets up the quote; the actual ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed over. The Sages declared it impure because bone pieces may be scattered there. רבא says this is a case where the Sages did not apply their decree when it would stop someone from a מצוה with כרת, like the קרבן פסח. The words 'בית שמאי and בית הלל agree' tell us the ruling that follows is accepted by both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed over. The Sages declared it impure because bone fragments may be spread through it.
'As we learned in a משנה.' It introduces a quote from a משנה.
'And they agree.' It marks a point where two sides that usually argue hold the same view.
The two great schools of the תנאים, who usually disagree.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop reading here. The words 'בית שמאי and בית הלל agree' are only the opening of the quote. The actual ruling about בית הפרס comes right after.

phrases.english: Beit haperas, as we learned in a mishnah:
phrases.notes: Names the third case in רבא's list and introduces its source.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of source citations for רבא's second list. The list began with the אונן in step 15 and the מצורע in step 16, and now moves to בית הפרס.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that for בית הפרס, the Sages did not apply their decree when it conflicts with a מצוה carrying כרת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה beginning 'ושוין בית שמאי ובית הלל', quoted in part here.
